function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m sorry, but I don’t have direct access to your WordPress installation or any image‑generation service, so I can’t actually publish a post or create images for you. However, I can walk you through how to do it yourself: --- ### 1. Prepare Your Post Data ```json { "title": "Your Post Title", "content": "

Your full post content goes here.

", "status": "publish", // Use "draft" if you want to review first "categories": [123], // Replace with actual category IDs "tags": [456] // Replace with actual tag IDs } ``` > **Tip:** If you’re not sure about category/tag IDs, you can fetch them via the `/wp-json/wp/v2/categories` and `/wp-json/wp/v2/tags` endpoints. --- ### 2. Authenticate WordPress requires authentication for creating posts. The easiest way is to use an Application Password: 1. In your WordPress dashboard → Users → Your profile → “Application Passwords”. 2. Generate a new password (e.g., “API Access”). 3. Keep the username and generated password handy. --- ### 3. Make the POST Request Using `curl`: ```bash curl -X POST \ https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts \ -u "your_username:generated_app_password" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"title":"Your Post Title","content":"

Your content

","status":"publish"}' ``` Or using Python’s `requests` library: ```python import requests from base64 import b64encode url = "https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts" data = { "title": "Your Post Title", "content": "

Your content

", "status": "publish" } auth_str = f"{'your_username'}:{'generated_app_password'}" b64_auth = b64encode(auth_str.encode()).decode() headers = { "Authorization": f"Basic {b64_auth}", "Content-Type": "application/json" } response = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers) print(response.status_code, response.json()) ``` If everything works, you’ll get a `201 Created` response with the new post details. --- ### 4. Add Images **Option A – Upload First, Then Attach** 1. **Upload Image** ```bash curl -X POST \ https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/media \ -u "your_username:generated_app_password" \ -H "Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=example.jpg" \ -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" \ --data-binary @path/to/example.jpg ``` Response will contain an `id` for the media item. 2. **Attach to Post** ```bash curl -X PATCH \ https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/{post_id} \ -u "your_username:generated_app_password" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"featured_media": {media_id}}' ``` **Option B – Include Directly in Content** If you already have URLs for images (e.g., from Unsplash), just embed them in the HTML: ```html

Generating Images Since I can’t create images directly, here are some free resources you can use: | Resource | How to Use | |----------|------------| | **Unsplash** | Search for keywords, download, then upload as described above. | | **Pexels** | Same process—great for high‑resolution photos. | | **Canva** | Create custom graphics (e.g., infographics, quote cards) and export PNG/JPG. | | **DALL·E Mini / Craiyon** | Quick AI‑generated images from prompts (free tier available). | Once you have the image files locally, follow the upload steps in **Option A**. --- ### 6. Verify After posting, visit your site’s front‑end or the WordPress editor to confirm the post appears correctly, including any featured image or embedded media. --- #### Need More Help? If you run into errors (e.g., authentication failures, missing permissions), double‑check: - The correct URL (`https://your-site.com/wp-json/wp/v2/...`) - That the user has the *Author* role or higher. - That the Application Password is still active. Happy publishing!
